Preferential independence: preferences on one criterion do not depend on the levels of the others, so an additive form is appropriate.
Partial values are normalised to [0, 1] over the stated scale range; weights are swing weights over those same ranges.

Classes are fixed boundaries on the overall value: an alternative belongs to the best class whose lower boundary it reaches, and a value within 1e-12 of a boundary goes to the higher class. Class membership inherits every MAVT assumption, including compensation.
result.weight_basis: Swing weights: each rating expresses the importance of the swing from the worst to the best level of that criterion over the stated scale range, not abstract importance. Changing a scale range changes the meaning of its weight.

assumptions: Net outranking flows compare the alternatives with one another: adding or removing an alternative can change every flow, and the order of two others. They are not preference values.

Each criterion compares the measurements of every pair through its stated preference function; a difference at or beyond the full-preference point counts the same however large it is, so a large advantage on one criterion offsets others only up to that point.
Weights are PROMETHEE's own importances, normalised by their sum; they are not swing weights, and value functions are not read.
A labelled criterion is compared on its stated codes; its differences and thresholds are in coded units.
Missing measurements are not imputed; the model must be complete to be evaluated.
result.label: net outranking flows: these compare the alternatives with one another and are not preference values
